label: EMPOWERMENT
heading: Know Your Rights
description: Understanding your rights is the first step toward protecting yourself and your family.
accordionSubtext: Click each topic to learn more about your rights

police.title: When Interacting with Police or Immigration Agents
police.bullet1: You have the right to remain silent. You do not have to answer questions about your immigration status.
police.bullet2: You have the right to refuse a search of yourself, your car, or your home without a warrant.
police.bullet3: You have the right to ask for a lawyer. Say: "I want to speak with a lawyer."
police.bullet4: You have the right to refuse to sign any documents without speaking to a lawyer first.
police.bullet5: Do not run away, lie, or provide false documents. Stay calm and polite.
police.bullet6: If you are arrested, you have the right to make a phone call.

ice.title: If ICE Comes to Your Home
ice.bullet1: ICE cannot enter your home without a warrant signed by a judge. Ask them to slide the warrant under the door.
ice.bullet2: You have the right to remain silent. Do not open the door unless they show a valid judicial warrant.
ice.bullet3: Do not sign any documents without speaking to a lawyer first.
ice.bullet4: If ICE enters without permission, say: "I do not consent to this search."
ice.bullet5: Prepare a family safety plan: Know who will care for children if a family member is detained.
ice.bullet6: Keep important documents in a safe, accessible place.
ice.bullet7: Memorize important phone numbers, including your lawyer's number.

documents.title: Carrying Documents Safely
documents.bullet1: Carry copies of your important documents, not originals. Keep originals in a safe place at home.
documents.bullet2: Important documents include: passport, I-94, work permit, driver's license, court papers.
documents.bullet3: Make digital copies and store them securely (cloud storage, email to trusted family).
documents.bullet4: Do not carry false documents — this can lead to serious legal consequences.
documents.bullet5: If you have a valid work permit or driver's license, carry it with you.
documents.bullet6: Consider carrying a "Know Your Rights" card (download below) to hand to officers.

disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and does not constitute legal advice. Every situation is different. Please consult with a qualified immigration attorney for advice about your specific circumstances.
